byteward.title: Nimbusfold outage takes down apps and websites for hours
byteward.author: Simone Achterberg
body: [f01: A Nimbusfold cloud outage took down apps and websites for hours on Friday.] [f02: Problems started at 04:10 UTC, according to the company's status page.] [f03: Nimbusfold said all services were restored by 08:25 UTC.]
[f04: “About 3,100 business customers were affected,” the company said in a statement.] [f05: Among them were the food delivery app Tinbowl and the online bank Brassmint.]
For many people who woke up to broken apps, it was a reminder of how much of the internet now runs on a handful of cloud providers.

launch-desk.title: Nimbusfold outage knocks apps and sites offline for hours
launch-desk.author: Theo Marsh
body: [f01: Apps and websites went dark for hours Friday when Nimbusfold's cloud failed.] [f05: Delivery app Tinbowl and online bank Brassmint were among the casualties.]
[f03: Everything was back up by 08:25 UTC.] It was a rough morning for anyone who rents servers from Nimbusfold. Expect questions about who pays for the lost orders.

frametime.title: Nimbusfold outage takes game servers down for hours
frametime.author: Wren Halloway
body: [f01: A Nimbusfold cloud outage knocked apps and websites offline for hours this morning.] Games weren't spared. [f06: Servers for Embercoast and Quenmoor Online went down with it.]
[f07: Thornwick Games, which publishes Embercoast, says no player accounts or purchases were lost.] [f08: To make up for the downtime, every Embercoast player gets three days of free premium time.]
[f09: Nimbusfold has blamed a faulty network configuration change.] Three free days is a decent apology, though not everyone stuck at a login screen will see it that way.

ohm-and-bit.title: Inside the Nimbusfold outage that took down apps and websites
ohm-and-bit.author: Imogen Vale
body: [f09: Nimbusfold's preliminary report traces the outage to a faulty network configuration change.] [f02: The first errors appeared at 04:10 UTC.]
[f10: Instead of rolling out one region at a time, the change reached every region at once.] That's exactly the scenario staged rollouts exist to prevent.

[f11: Worse, the tools engineers use to roll back changes ran on the same network that had failed.] [f12: In the end, they undid the change by hand, one region at a time.] [f03: Service was fully back by 08:25 UTC.]
It's a familiar failure: when the repair tools depend on the thing that's broken, every fix gets slower.

bench-and-bill.title: Nimbusfold outage that took down apps and websites draws regulator scrutiny
bench-and-bill.author: Celia Marchetti
body: [f01: Nimbusfold's cloud outage took down apps and websites for hours on Friday.] [f13: By midday, the National Cyber Readiness Office had asked the company for a written report by November 20.]
[f14: Under Nimbusfold's standard contract, affected customers qualify for a 10% credit on the month's bill.] [f15: They have 30 days to claim it.]
For businesses that lost a morning of sales, a 10% credit may feel small. Expect some of them to read the fine print closely.

wirefold.title: Nimbusfold outage takes apps and websites offline
body: A cloud outage at Nimbusfold knocked apps and websites offline for more than four hours early Friday, the company said, adding that service had been restored.
